subtitle: When a Vassal Learned Where the Walls Were Thin

panels.shot: epic split composition, one half a crumbling Rashtrakuta throne, the other a rising Western Chalukya banner over the Deccan
panels.action: Tailapa II stands firm with a Chalukya-style banner, while Karka II sits uneasy on a worn Rashtrakuta throne amid dust and fading grandeur of Manyakheta.

dialogue.text: In 972–973 CE, as Manyakheta lay shaken by a northern raid, Tailapa II, once a Rashtrakuta vassal, moved against Karka II—and a two‑century Deccan empire fell into the dust.

i18n.hi: ९७२–९७३ ईस्वी में, उत्तर के हमले से हिला मन्यखेता… तभी पूर्व आश्रित तैलप द्वितीय ने कार्क द्वितीय पर वार किया—और दो सौ साल पुराना दक्खनी साम्राज्य धूल में गिर पड़ा।

panels.shot: wide aerial over the Deccan plateau at dusk
panels.action: The Deccan heartland stretches under a fading sky, rivers glinting, ancient trade routes threading toward the fortified city of Manyakheta on the horizon.

dialogue.text: For two hundred years, the Rashtrakutas ruled this plateau. Arab geographers knew their Balhara court; merchants crossed oceans under their shadow.

i18n.hi: दो सौ बरस तक इस पठार पर राष्ट्रकूटों की हुकूमत थी। अरब भूगोलवेत्ता उनके बलहारा दरबार को जानते थे; सौदागर उनकी छाया में समंदर पार करते थे।

panels.shot: interior wide of the Rashtrakuta durbar in its prime
panels.action: Karka II, younger and tense, sits on an ornate Rashtrakuta throne in Manyakheta’s hall, while courtiers and vassal envoys, including a watchful Tailapa II at the edge, stand amidst carved pillars.

dialogue.text: In Manyakheta, the Balhara throne passed to Karka II, heir to a line that had faced Gurjara‑Pratiharas, Palas and Cholas. Yet the hall no longer rang with unstoppable power.

i18n.hi: मन्यखेता में बलहारा सिंहासन कार्क द्वितीय को मिला, उस वंशज को जिसने गुर्जर–प्रतिहार, पाल और चोलों का सामना किया था। पर सभा अब अजेय गूँज से खाली थी।

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot of a Paramara war band riding south
panels.action: Paramara horsemen led by Siyaka thunder along a dusty route toward the Deccan, banners whipping, armor plain but determined, the landscape growing drier and stony.

dialogue.text: From Malwa, the Paramara ruler Siyaka rode south. His inscriptions would later boast: he reached Manyakheta, Rashtrakuta capital, and sacked it.

i18n.hi: मालवा से परमार नरेश सियाका दक्षिण कूदा। आगे चलकर उसके शिलालेख गर्व से बोले: वह राष्ट्रकूट राजधानी मन्यखेता तक पहुंचा और उसे लूटा।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Manyakheta’s walls under assault
panels.action: Manyakheta’s stone ramparts tremble as siege engines batter the gates, fires smolder in outer quarters, and defenders stand scattered atop the battlements amid rising dust.

dialogue.text: The Rashtrakuta copper plates fall silent at this wound. Paramara records speak instead: Manyakheta was struck, its pride shaken, its resources drained.

i18n.hi: उस घाव पर राष्ट्रकूट ताम्रपट्ट चुप हो जाते हैं। परमार अभिलेख बोलते हैं: मन्यखेता पर चोट पड़ी, अभिमान डगमगाया, संपदा सूख गई।

panels.shot: somber interior of a damaged palace
panels.action: Inside a hall scarred by smoke and disrepair, Karka II consults anxious ministers, while Tailapa II, as a regional chief, observes the cracked pillars and strained faces in steady silence.

dialogue.text: From outside, the blow looked brief. From within, it was deeper: treasuries lighter, troops lost, allies uncertain. Vassals saw the cracks in the great house.

i18n.hi: बाहर से यह वार क्षणिक लगा। भीतर से वह गहरा था: खज़ाने हल्के, सेनाएँ घटीं, सहयोगी दुविधा में। आश्रितों ने महान घर में दरारें देख लीं।

panels.shot: medium shot in a smaller provincial court
panels.action: Tailapa II sits in his own modest but well‑kept hall in the western Deccan, paler banners behind him, listening as a messenger from Manyakheta brings demands for loyalty and levies.

dialogue.text: One of these vassals was Tailapa II, ruling in the western Deccan. His grants later traced a Chalukya heritage and spoke of old rights and new ambitions.

i18n.hi: इन आश्रितों में एक था तैलप द्वितीय, जो पश्चिमी दक्खन पर शासन करता था। उसके दानपत्र पुराने चालुक्य वंश और नई चाह की कहानी लिखते हैं।

panels.shot: close two-shot, Tailapa in foreground, image of Karka blurred behind
panels.action: Tailapa II’s face is lit by lamplight as he studies a palm‑leaf grant, the faint figure of Karka II on a distant throne imagined behind him, symbolizing the suzerain he serves.

dialogue.text: The Balhara lion stumbles. Is this the hour for the old Chalukya claim?

i18n.hi: बलहारा का सिंह लड़खड़ाया। क्या यह घड़ी है पुराने चालुक्य हक़ की?

panels.shot: slow push-in on a copper plate inscription being engraved
panels.action: An artisan carefully engraves Sanskrit letters onto a gleaming copper plate, while a priest and scribe supervise, scrolls beside them bearing Tailapa’s royal titles.

dialogue.text: Tailapa’s own copper plates, from Kauthem and beyond, name him lord, link him to ancient Chalukyas, and quietly declare a throne apart from Rashtrakuta grace.

i18n.hi: कौठेम और आगे के तैलप के ताम्रपट्ट उसे स्वामी कहते हैं, उसे प्राचीन चालुक्यों से जोड़ते हैं, और चुपचाप राष्ट्रकूट कृपा से अलग एक सिंहासन घोषित करते हैं।

panels.shot: wide outdoor shot of Tailapa’s forces assembling
panels.action: Tailapa II rides at the head of a disciplined column of Deccan cavalry and infantry, banners showing his emblems, moving through scrubland toward the east where Manyakheta lies.

dialogue.text: Between 972 and 973, as inscriptions shift, Tailapa moved. Not in a single glorious duel, but in a campaign that pushed aside weakened Rashtrakuta authority.

i18n.hi: ९७२–९७३ के बीच, जब लेख बदलने लगे, तैलप ने चाल चली। कोई एक महिमा–युद्ध नहीं, बल्कि ऐसा अभियान जिसने कमजोर राष्ट्रकूट सत्ता को किनारे कर दिया।

panels.shot: tense mid-shot of Karka II on the battlements
panels.action: Karka II, armor hastily donned, stands on a city wall overlooking Tailapa’s approaching banners, his face set but burdened, advisors nervous around him.

dialogue.speaker: tailapa_ii_and_karka_ii
dialogue.text: A vassal knows his master’s strengths—and his forgotten outposts.

i18n.hi: आश्रित अपने स्वामी की ताकत भी जानता है—और उसके भूले चौकियाँ भी।

panels.shot: wide shot of opposing armies facing each other across a dusty plain
panels.action: On a broad plain, Tailapa II’s arrayed forces stand firm opposite a smaller, uneven Rashtrakuta host under Karka II’s banner, dust hanging as both sides hold in charged silence.

dialogue.text: Ranna, the Kannada poet at Tailapa’s court, would later sing of fierce battle. His Gadayuddham praises his patron, but behind the poetry lies a clear change of masters.

i18n.hi: तैलप के दरबार का कन्नड़ कवि रण्णा बाद में भीषण युद्ध गाएगा। उसका गदयुद्धम अपने नायक की स्तुति करता है, पर पंक्तियों के पीछे राज–परिवर्तन साफ़ झलकता है।

panels.shot: dramatic but restrained mid-shot of Tailapa entering Manyakheta
panels.action: Tailapa II rides through the main gate of Manyakheta, now subdued, his standard raised; Karka II is absent, the streets lined by watchful townsfolk and new guards.

dialogue.text: What we do not see in records are details of every clash. What we do see is outcome: Tailapa II in power, Karka II gone, Manyakheta under new rule.

i18n.hi: हर भिड़ंत का ब्यौरा लेखों में नहीं। पर नतीजा दिखता है: तैलप द्वितीय गद्दी पर, कार्क द्वितीय गायब, मन्यखेता नए शासक के नीचे।

panels.shot: low-angle interior shot of Tailapa seated on the former Rashtrakuta throne
panels.action: In the same grand hall once held by Rashtrakutas, Tailapa II now sits on the central throne, courtiers reorganized around him, old Rashtrakuta emblems partially removed.

dialogue.text: From this seat grew the Western Chalukyas of Kalyani. Inscription by inscription, their name rose where Rashtrakuta titles fell silent.

i18n.hi: यहीं से कल्याणी के पश्चिमी चालुक्य उठे। शिलालेख–दर–शिलालेख, उनका नाम चढ़ा जहाँ राष्ट्रकूट उपाधियाँ मौन हुईं।

panels.shot: map-style wide showing shifting spheres of influence
panels.action: A stylized map of India shows the Deccan, former Rashtrakuta zone fading, a new Western Chalukya color spreading, while Paramara Malwa and other powers hold their regions.

dialogue.text: The Deccan’s balance changed. Where Arab geographers had written of Balharas, later travelers and grants would speak instead of Chalukyas in Kalyani.

i18n.hi: दक्खन का संतुलन बदल गया। जहाँ अरब लेखकों ने बलहारों को लिखा था, बाद के यात्रियों और दानपत्रों ने कल्याणी के चालुक्यों का नाम दर्ज किया।

panels.shot: quiet interior of Tailapa’s court with poet Ranna reciting
panels.action: In a calmer Kalyani court, the poet Ranna stands reciting to assembled nobles, while Tailapa listens, the mood one of self‑confident consolidation after turmoil.

dialogue.text: Ranna’s verses, tailored to praise, still carry a historian’s gift: they remember Siyaka’s blow, Tailapa’s ascent, and the sense that an old age had ended.

i18n.hi: रण्णा के स्तुति–गीत भी इतिहास की भेंट हैं: वे सियाका के वार, तैलप की चढ़त और बीते युग के अंत की धड़कन याद रखते हैं।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from a weathered Rashtrakuta emblem lying in dust
panels.action: A carved Rashtrakuta emblem lies half‑buried at the base of a wall, worn by time; in the distance, newer Chalukya symbols hang from steady towers.

dialogue.text: The Rashtrakutas did not fall in one glorious duel. They fell when a northern enemy struck their heart, and an old servant, knowing the thin walls, claimed the house.

i18n.hi: राष्ट्रकूट किसी एक वीर–युद्ध में नहीं गिरे। वे तब गिरे, जब उत्तर का दुश्मन उनके दिल पर वार कर गया, और पुराना सेवक, पतली दीवारें जानकर, पूरे घर पर दावा कर बैठा।

panels.shot: reflective medium shot of Tailapa on a balcony overlooking the Deccan
panels.action: Tailapa II stands on a balcony, looking over the Deccan plains at sunset, Karka II’s faded banner stored inside, symbolizing the empire he replaced.

dialogue.text: Tailapa II and Karka II remind us: empires are most fragile when those who once served them learn where they have grown hollow—and choose to step through the dust.

i18n.hi: तैलप द्वितीय और कार्क द्वितीय हमें याद दिलाते हैं: साम्राज्य सबसे नाज़ुक तब होते हैं, जब पुराने सेवक उनकी खोखली दीवारें पहचान लेते हैं—और धूल में कदम रखकर भीतर आ जाते हैं।

title_i18n.en: The Dynasty That Fell in the Dust
title_i18n.hi: धूल में बिखरी एक वंश कथा

subtitle_i18n.en: When a Vassal Learned Where the Walls Were Thin
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब आश्रित ने पहचान ली कमज़ोर दीवारें
